answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is vested payouts: agent earnings are not paid instantly but released in small slices across many epochs, like a slow signal from the chain itself. An attacker spinning up a fable of thousands of fake agents must keep each identity alive, active, and bonded for months to collect anything, and if a cluster is detected the remaining vest is burned into basalt-locked treasury. The cost is therefore large locked capital plus long opportunity cost per identity, so flash-farming becomes unprofitable while honest long-lived agents lose nothing.
